quickAnswerHtml: Hok Kee Lao is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in Phang-Nga, in the Takua Pa Old Town area. Budget around THB 101–250 per person, and it's mostly walk-in / queue at the door — it closes for part of the year, so check before you go

blocks.html:
Mention Takua Pa Old Town and most people picture the Sino-Portuguese shophouses and the quiet heritage street. But locals in Phang-Nga will give you another name right away: "Hok Kee Lao," an old Thai-Chinese restaurant that's been open for more than 40 years in a two-storey shophouse in the middle of Takua Pa. Step inside and you still get that old-school Chinese-restaurant feel that's getting harder to find — big round tables, dishes brought out one by one for the whole table to share, the same way Takua Pa's Chinese families have eaten for generations. Takua Pa was once a booming tin-mining town, and the Chinese migrants who came to work the mines brought Southern Chinese food culture with them, a tradition that's stayed rooted here ever since. Hok Kee Lao is one of the restaurants still carrying that flavor forward today.

MICHELIN has awarded this restaurant a Bib Gourmand for several years running, from around 2022 through the 2026 guide, for a reason that's refreshingly simple: it's a family-gathering restaurant with a consistent hand in the kitchen — no gambling on whether today's meal will be good. The dish MICHELIN singles out is the soy-braised free-range chicken served with water spinach — firm free-range chicken blanched just right, dressed in the restaurant's own soy sauce recipe, and eaten with blanched water spinach that needs nothing else added. The other standout is the loaded tofu — fried tofu with minced pork and shrimp, a dish the kids at the table tend to claim before anyone else gets a chance. And the crab noodle rolls, minced pork mixed with shrimp meat and deep-fried, make an easy, moreish snack while you wait for the mains.

Two more dishes worth trying are the crab tube noodles and the dry-fried fish maw — both Chinese-style dishes that take real skill and that most restaurants simply don't offer. Eating them in a restaurant this old feels different from eating them anywhere else. Anyone driving the Khao Lak-Takua Pa route, or wandering the old town for photos, will find this restaurant a worthwhile stop for lunch or dinner if you plan your timing right — per-person prices sit in the low hundreds, but you're eating Chinese cooking at a level MICHELIN has kept vouching for year after year, in a small Andaman-coast town that most people just drive through.

blocks.name: Hok Kee Lao
blocks.descHtml:
Hok Kee Lao is in Takua Pa, near the big market, across from the Esso station — easy to find. Prices run about THB 101–250 per person, easy on the wallet for a Bib Gourmand restaurant, but according to MICHELIN the restaurant only takes cash, so bring enough. It's open every day, split into two sittings: 10:30-13:30 and 16:30-21:30. The restaurant closes for a break from 13:30-16:30 — don't show up then, you'll find it shut.

It's mostly walk-in, but if you're coming as a large group or visiting for a busy holiday lunch, it's worth calling ahead at +66 76 421 938 or the backup number 081-891-2296 — the restaurant only takes bookings by phone. There's an air-conditioned room upstairs, good for larger family groups. The most convenient way there is by car — it's not far up Phetkasem Road from Khao Lak, so you can stop for a meal and then walk around Takua Pa Old Town afterward. Dress is casual, no rules there. The easiest time to go is a weekday dinner — the evening sitting runs until 9:30pm.

faq.a: Normally you can just walk in, but for a large group or a busy holiday lunch, it's worth calling ahead at +66 76 421 938 or the backup number 081-891-2296 — the restaurant only takes bookings by phone, no online booking
Around THB 101–250 per person, very cheap for a Bib Gourmand restaurant, but according to MICHELIN the restaurant only takes cash, so bring enough cash with you

faq.q: What should I order at Hok Kee Lao?
faq.a: The dishes MICHELIN highlights are the soy-braised free-range chicken with water spinach and the loaded tofu. The crab noodle rolls, crab tube noodles, and dry-fried fish maw are also standouts worth ordering to share across the table

faq.q: What are the hours, and when's the best time to go?
faq.a: Open every day in two sittings, 10:30-13:30 and 16:30-21:30. Watch out for the afternoon break from 13:30-16:30 when the restaurant is closed. Holiday lunches get crowded, so a weekday dinner is more comfortable. The restaurant is in Takua Pa, near the big market, across from the Esso station, with an air-conditioned room upstairs
